sections.what: Creates three users and a helper that reads a crew's invite code.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: crews: create, invite, join, leave
sections.title: Create, join, leave and owner rules
sections.what: Checks crews are private, joining and leaving works, owners can rotate codes and remove members, ownership must be handed over before leaving, and the database has no money columns or league tables.
sections.why: Likely reason: crews are free and owner controlled, and the money check guards against old league fields returning.
sections.watch_out: The money check looks for name patterns, so it can miss a column with a different name.

sections.name: crews: invite links
sections.title: Invite links opened twice or at once
sections.what: Checks a second open returns the crew without joining again, a bad code is not found, and several simultaneous opens create one membership.
sections.why: Likely reason: people often click the same link more than once, so repeat opens must not fail.
sections.watch_out: The concurrency guarantee depends on the database stopping duplicate memberships.

summary: Tests the crew lifecycle: private creation, joining and leaving, owner control over the invite code and members, ownership handover, a check that money columns are gone, and invite links that work even when opened twice or at once.
purpose: Protects how crews are created, joined, left and managed.
why: Likely reason: crews are private and owner controlled, and the money check guards against old league fee columns coming back.
how: Creates three users and a helper to read invite codes. Checks a new crew is private with a six-character code. Checks join then leave. Checks the owner can rotate the code and remove members, while others cannot, and old codes stop working. Checks an owner must hand over before leaving, and the last owner leaving deletes the crew. Checks the database has no fee or prize-type columns and no league tables. Checks opening a link twice returns the crew the second time. Checks four simultaneous opens create one membership and open the crew for all.
inputs: Test users, crews created during the tests, and the database.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The money-column check uses a name pattern, so a new column with a different name would not be caught. The concurrent-join test assumes the database prevents duplicate memberships.
debug: If a permission test fails, check the owner check in the crew service. If the concurrency test fails, check the membership uniqueness in the database.
